references.text: The law that those who are unclean because of a dead body must be sent outside the camp, which explains why these men were concerned about their uncleanness.
The Nazirite law regarding uncleanness from dead bodies, showing that contact with the dead made a person unclean.
Detailed laws concerning uncleanness from touching a dead body and the cleansing process required.
Priests were not to make themselves unclean by the dead, demonstrating the seriousness of uncleanness associated with death.
The consequence of failing to celebrate Passover while clean, highlighting the importance of participating in the Passover celebration.
The command that the entire congregation of Israel must celebrate Passover, explaining the men's desire not to be excluded.
